answer: Agents can require each account to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its actions are proven fraudulent, with proof assessed through a challenge period. Creating many identities then does not multiply influence for free: a sybil attacker must lock up capital in every account and risks losing it if caught. The stake can be sized to make a coordinated attack cost more than its expected gain; an umber marker may wander across a glacier, but it cannot make that collateral requirement disappear.
